note: The A5 fixed evaluation: six questions at the web lanes, the wording FROZEN (the seeker's words ride as spoken). The expected-lane words were written from a live search-level probe of the day BEFORE the run (an expectation, never a score). Scoring rides SEPARATE axes (no one number); the machine fills retrieval/traceability/independence words, the OPERATOR (the A5 hand, same brain that wrote the code - disclosed, not independent) fills the review axes after inspecting the answer against the bytes that reached the mouth. Absent axes read UNREVIEWED, never a silent pass.

questions.question: Ashoka rock edict
questions.expect: an origin abstract + a read origin page; ONE origin voice (independence none by law); this question IS the A4 bytes (web-run-1) - the A4-to-A5 comparison rides here

questions.question: Magna Carta
questions.expect: the provider may answer by ITS OWN house stubs alone (attribution-only shape); an exact 1215 is then NOT in the bytes that reached the mouth - an unsourced date must show on the citation-support axis, not acquire false DOCUMENTED airs

questions.question: Krishna
questions.expect: a disambiguation-shaped answer (many referents): conflict rides UNRESOLVED at the packet (the provider's bytes carry no edges); the answer must not pick a referent and call it fact

questions.question: Zzzyx plingworth

questions.question: Upanishad
questions.expect: an origin definitional sentence (documented: what the texts verifiably are) while any READING of them rides the mouth's own voice (interpretation); the answer must keep the two apart

questions.question: Kalama Sutta
questions.expect: the P7 experiment: one text with genuinely different interpretive traditions (Buddhist exegesis, scholarly reading, modern appropriation); an accessible origin source exists; the answer must separate the text's words, a tradition's reading, scholarship, and what the sources cannot settle; convergence is a hypothesis, not a result
